findings.title: TOCTOU race allows device limit to be exceeded
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first calls CountDevices to check whether the configured deviceLimit has been reached, then, if under limit, runs an unconditional INSERT...ON CONFLICT. These two operations run in separate sessions with no locking, so under concurrent anonymous authentications several requests can all observe count < deviceLimit and proceed to insert new rows, exceeding the configured limit by however many requests race in the same window. With limit=10 a burst of new device IDs can easily push the table to 12-15 active devices. The limit cannot be safely enforced in application code in this shape; it needs either a single atomic statement (e.g. INSERT ... SELECT with a count check in a CTE, plus a database transaction), a row-level lock, or a unique constraint plus a DB trigger.

findings.title: localCache is set before the DB call, so ErrDeviceLimitReached is silently bypassed on the next request
findings.body: tagDeviceUI writes a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{}) before invoking CreateOrUpdateDevice and returns nil on cache hit. Combined with the new ErrDeviceLimitReached returned by the store, this means: the first request from a brand-new device when the limit is reached sets the cache and fails authentication; the very next request from the same device within the 29 minute cache TTL hits the cache, tagDeviceUI returns nil, TagDevice returns nil, and Authenticate returns a valid identity. The device limit is therefore defeated simply by retrying once. The cache entry needs to either track failure (return the cached error on subsequent hits, or only populate the cache after a successful tag) so the rejection is enforced for the full TTL.

findings.title: Synchronous DB write and removed panic recovery in the anonymous auth path is a regression
findings.body: The previous implementation invoked TagDevice from a goroutine with a panic recover and a 2-minute timeout, so anonymous authentication never blocked on a DB write. This PR removes the goroutine and the recover and calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context. Every anonymous request now performs an INSERT/UPDATE in the auth hot path: DB latency directly adds to login latency, a slow or unreachable DB will deny anonymous logins instead of just losing the tag, and any panic inside TagDevice now propagates to the auth handler. This is a notable behavior change that the description and reviewer checklist do not call out.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as number | undefined but the backend always emits a number
findings.body: The Go DTO declares AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 (non-pointer, no omitempty), so the /api/frontend/settings endpoint always serializes a number, never omits the field. The TypeScript field anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined plus the runtime default anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined are inconsistent with this: the frontend will always receive a concrete number (0 for unlimited, or the configured value), and never undefined. Either change the DTO to *int64 with omitempty to truly support undefined, or fix the TS types/defaults to number with 0 default so the contract matches what the API actually sends.

findings.title: No test exercises the concurrency path that the new check/enforce split relies on
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only runs two sequential CreateOrUpdateDevice calls. The whole correctness story of the limit hinges on the check-then-insert in CreateOrUpdateDevice being safe under concurrent load, and on the local cache correctly handling ErrDeviceLimitReached on retry. Neither is covered: there is no parallel test that fires N goroutines with unique device IDs against a small limit and asserts the resulting count, and no test that calls CreateOrUpdateDevice twice with a cache layer to assert that the second call after ErrDeviceLimitReached still returns the error. Without these, the race and the cache-bypass bugs above can regress silently.

findings.title: New auth.anonymous.device_limit setting has no documentation or sample
findings.body: The PR adds cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit = anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0) but does not update the configuration documentation (e.g. docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/_index.md or the sample config under conf/defaults.ini) to describe the new key, its default (0 = unlimited), the 30-day activity window, or the new behavior that hitting the limit will reject anonymous logins. The reviewer checklist explicitly asks to confirm docs are updated and this is not done. Users will have no way to discover or understand the setting, and operators who turn it on will be surprised that anonymous access starts returning errors when the limit is hit.
